analysis.title: TJX Cos. (TJX): F3Q27 First Take: Better-than-feared 3Q as Marmaxx improves, FY comp outlook raised
key_insights: TJX reported F3Q27 adjusted EPS of $1.34, which excludes a $0.05 net benefit from IEEPA tariff refunds. That is in line with GS consensus of $1.33 and FactSet consensus of $1.34.

Total comps were +4%, against GS at +2.8% and consensus at +2.9%. Marmaxx comps were +2%, HomeGoods +5%, TJX Canada +6% and TJX International +8%. Net sales rose 6% Y/Y against GS/consensus of +4.5%/+4.6%.
Marmaxx comps improved to +2% from +1% in F2Q, and management expects further improvement in F4Q. GS calls this the most important element of the print.

Adjusted gross margin was 32.1%, below GS at 32.2% and consensus at 32.4%. Management cited higher freight and fuel costs. Adjusted SG&A was 19.8% of sales against 20.0%/20.1% expected, which lifted adjusted pretax margin to 12.5% against 12.3% expected.

TJX raised its FY27 comp outlook to +4% from +3%-4% and narrowed adjusted EPS guidance to $5.17-$5.20 from $5.15-$5.20. The new range excludes an expected $0.16 net benefit from tariff refunds. It sits below GS/FactSet consensus of $5.22/$5.25.

The F4Q outlook is below consensus on comps, margin and EPS. Guidance is comps of +2%-3%, adjusted pretax margin of 11.8%-11.9% and adjusted EPS of $1.42-$1.45, against consensus of +3.1%/+3.0%, 11.9%/11.8% and $1.48. The 4Q margin and EPS outlook now assume additional fuel costs.

Unseasonably warm weather in the US and Canada weighed on demand in some categories. Management expects sales momentum to accelerate through the holiday season and describes merchandise availability as outstanding.

GS expects call commentary to focus on four points: Marmaxx drivers and F4Q expectations, the size and duration of freight and fuel pressure including carryover into next fiscal year, holiday trends against the weather pressure, and the sustainability of comps outside Marmaxx (HomeGoods and International).
Inventory rose 5.2% Y/Y against GS at +5.9%. Per store, inventory was flat on a reported basis and flat ex-FX. Quarter-end cash was $4.6bn.
GS maintains a Buy rating and a $178 12-month price target based on 19.0x Q5-Q8 EV/EBITDA. The target is unchanged from the 19-Aug-26 level, and the stock closed at $129.85 on 17 Nov 2026.

market_movers.rationale: Buy and $178 target (19.0x Q5-Q8 EV/EBITDA) kept after a print GS views as better than feared. Comps beat and Marmaxx improved, while F4Q guidance is modestly light and gross margin missed slightly on fuel costs.

earnings_insights: TJX F3Q27 adjusted EPS $1.34 reported 11/18, excluding a $0.05 net benefit from IEEPA tariff refunds (partly offset by incremental compensation accruals). GS consensus est $1.33, FactSet consensus est $1.34. GAAP EPS was $1.39 against GS est $1.39.
F3Q27 total comp sales +4% reported against GS est +2.8% and consensus est +2.9%. Net sales $15,952mn, +6% Y/Y, against GS est $15,803.9mn.

F3Q27 adjusted gross margin 32.1% reported against GS est 32.2% and consensus est 32.4%. Adjusted SG&A 19.8% of sales against GS est 20.0% and consensus est 20.1%. Adjusted pretax margin 12.5% against GS/consensus est 12.3%.

FY27 guidance: adjusted EPS $5.17-$5.20 excluding an expected $0.16 net benefit from tariff refunds, against $5.15-$5.20 prior and GS/FactSet consensus est $5.22/$5.25. Comps +4% against +3%-4% prior. Adjusted pretax margin unchanged at 12.0%-12.1% against GS/consensus est 11.9%/12.0%.

F4Q27 guidance: comps +2%-3%, adjusted pretax margin 11.8%-11.9%, adjusted EPS $1.42-$1.45, against GS/FactSet consensus est +3.1%/+3.0%, 11.9%/11.8% and $1.48. The guide assumes additional fuel costs versus prior guidance.
risk_factors: Deceleration in comparable-store sales, including slower store traffic.
Higher-than-anticipated disruption in the international business from geopolitical tension or macro volatility.
Slower margin expansion from weaker supply, ongoing inflationary pressure or other headwinds.
Higher freight and fuel costs, with possible carryover into next fiscal year.
Unseasonably warm US and Canada weather weighing on demand in some categories.
geopolitical: GS lists higher-than-anticipated disruption in TJX's international business from geopolitical tension or macro volatility as a key downside risk.
IEEPA tariff refunds benefit TJX's reported F3Q27 results and are excluded from adjusted figures.

tension_points.bull_case: Comps beat (+4% against +2.8%/+2.9%), Marmaxx improved to +2%, HomeGoods and International stayed strong, SG&A leverage lifted pretax margin to 12.5%, and the FY27 comp outlook was raised to +4%.
tension_points.bear_case: F4Q guidance is modestly light on comps, margin and EPS ($1.42-$1.45 against $1.48 consensus). Gross margin missed on freight and fuel costs, and warm weather weighed on some categories. FY27 adjusted EPS guidance sits below consensus.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Deceleration in comparable-store sales, including slower store traffic, which GS lists as the first key downside risk.

theme_stances.key_argument: Consolidated comps beat, Marmaxx improved and HomeGoods and International stayed strong, though the F4Q outlook is modestly light.
theme_stances.evidence: we view the print as better than feared
